sets.relationshipLabel: two counterparts of the same kind, named together
sets.explanation: Rain and shine, wet and dry — each pair names a familiar pair of opposites that travel together as a set phrase.

sets.relationshipLabel: a stretch of time and the weather-scent it produces
sets.explanation: A dry season kicks up dust just as monsoon rain releases petrichor — each stretch of time carries its own signature smell.

sets.relationshipLabel: storm system and its characteristic named feature
sets.explanation: A cumulonimbus cloud's flat top is its anvil, just as a supercell's rotating core is its mesocyclone — each storm system carries a signature named part.

sets.relationshipLabel: a warning sign and the weather event it foretells
sets.explanation: A barometric drop precedes a downpour and a green sky precedes hail — each is a sign that points toward, without guaranteeing, the event it warns of.
